content.text: second-line: VED, self-injected intracavernosal injections or intraurethral PGE1; self-administered intraurethral or intracavernosal alprostadil gives erections lasting a mean 30 to 60 min; intracavernous alprostadil may be compounded w papaverine and phentolamine; intraurethral is less effective than injection; adding it to a PDE5 inhibitor may help pts who fail a PDE5 inhibitor alone.

Alprostadil (Caverject) intracavernosal dose (vasculogenic, psychogenic or mixed ED): start 2.5 mcg; partial response: another 2.5 mcg w.in 1 h (new vial each dose); during titration ≤ 2 doses per 24 h; further titration in 5 to 10 mcg steps ≥ 24 h apart; target: an erection suitable for intercourse lasting ≤ 1 h; doses > 60 mcg ⍉ recommended. Home use: ≤ 3 times weekly, ≥ 24 h between doses. CI: conditions predisposing to priapism (sickle cell anemia or trait, multiple myeloma, leukemia); fibrotic conditions of the penis (angulation, cavernosal fibrosis, Peyronie dz); penile implants. Erection > 4 h: seek immediate medical help (untreated priapism → tissue damage, permanent loss of potency). Penile fibrosis (3% overall; 7.8% in an up-to-18-month self-injection study): examine the penis periodically; stop if angulation or cavernosal fibrosis develops. Can cause hypotension: ⍉ in known cavernosal venous leakage. Anticoagulants (warfarin, heparin): injection-site bleeding; compress the site for 5 min. Combos w other intracavernosal vasoactive agents: safety and efficacy not established; ↑ risk of prolonged erection, priapism and hypotension.
